title: Crochet for left-handers
subtitle: How to mirror right-handed instructions and read patterns as a left-handed crocheter
excerpt: Left-handed crochet is a mirror of the right-handed technique. The moves are identical; the hands are swapped. Here is how to translate any pattern.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

glossaryTerms.definition: The action of passing the working yarn over the hook from back to front, forming a loop that the hook then draws through.
The length of yarn attached to the ball or skein that you actively use to form stitches, as distinct from yarn tails or already-worked sections.

content.text: Left-handed crochet is a mirror image of right-handed crochet. The hook goes in the left hand, the yarn feeds through the right hand, and the work progresses from left to right instead of right to left. Every stitch, every move, and every pattern instruction is the same, but reversed.
What changes and what stays the same
What changes: the hook hand (left), the yarn hand (right), the direction the work travels across a row (left to right), the side the turning chain sits on at the end of a row.
What stays the same: all stitch names and abbreviations, all stitch counts, all increase and decrease instructions, hook sizes, yarn weights, gauge.
The yarn over direction
The
yarn over
is the same physical move but in the opposite horizontal direction. In right-handed crochet the
working yarn

swings over the hook from the back of the hook to the front (right to left). In left-handed crochet, it swings from back to front in the mirrored direction (left to right). The result is the same: a loop forms on the hook.
Reading right-handed instructions
Almost all written patterns assume a right-handed worker. Reading them as a left-hander is straightforward:
Stitch counts: identical. Work the same number of stitches.
Charts: read the row direction in reverse. A right-handed chart reads odd rows right to left; a left-hander reads those same rows left to right.
Shaping: instructions for 'right-hand side' and 'left-hand side' of a garment are reversed for a left-handed worker.
Learning from right-handed video
Mirror the video on screen if the platform has a flip option, or sit with the video playing while facing a mirror.
Watch the full sequence once, then replay it in sections and mirror each move in your own hands.
Ignore any reference to 'left side' or 'right side' in the commentary and substitute the opposite.
Common problems

items.cause: The yarn over is being worked in the same direction as a right-handed crocheter, so the twist in each loop goes the wrong way for the left hand.
items.fix: Check that the yarn over goes over the hook in the direction away from you (back to front in the mirror direction). The loop should sit cleanly on the hook with no crossing over.

items.symptom: Stitch counts are correct but the fabric looks tighter on one side
items.cause: The turning chain is being placed on the wrong side after mirroring.
items.fix: The turning chain should sit on the left edge of the completed row. If it is ending up on the right, you are turning the work in the wrong direction.

content.text: What to try next

Work the same foundation swatch right-handed crocheters use: a 20-stitch by 10-row rectangle in double crochet. Get the mirrored yarn-over direction consistent across all ten rows before moving on to other stitches.
